value.rules_markdown:
- Organize `src/` as single crate: one responsibility per module, core types in module-local `types.rs`, one trait per file in `src/ports/`.
- Declare every CLI subcommand in `src/bin/tinysweeper.rs` even if milestone not landed; `src/server/` is the only production surface.
- Store review policy as data in `presets/`: each preset is a folder with `preset.toml`, `README.md`, optional prompt overrides; never add a module for a preset.
- Treat `vendor/tinyagents` as a git submodule: never edit it here; change upstream and bump the pin.
- Keep one document per `src/` module at `docs/modules/<module>/README.md`.
- Declare examples in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features` so credential-needing smoke tests never build in CI.
- Default build is offline; link no HTTP client, test suite never touches network; network features must be gated (`harness`, `github`, `serve`).
- Follow rustfmt output and Rust 2024 idioms; use `snake_case` for modules/files, `PascalCase` for types.
- Return `Result<T>` using crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Start every file with a `//!` module doc describing role and any feature gating.
- Write comments that explain decisions, not code; call out load-bearing flags/ordering and why.
- Add doc comments to public items; use `///` on Clap fields so it becomes help text.
- Keep tests in-crate: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at bottom, move to sibling `test.rs` or `<name>_test.rs` when large; no `tests/` directory.
- Provide always-compiled offline mock for every port; `MockForge` records intended writes for exact assertions.
- Cover lane behaviour with golden tests: fixture diff + canned structured model response, asserting findings after filtering, dedupe, capping.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file, including guidelines, at 500 lines or fewer; split and link from module README.
- Security: model never holds write token; write credentials minted only in `src/apply/` after all model calls return; leaving a change fails.
- Security: never execute contributor code; read diff/tree only, no build, install, or running target repo scripts.
- Security: treat PR bodies/comments/diffs as untrusted input, fence and label as data; model verdict advisory; only `src/apply/` and `src/automerge/` may mutate GitHub.
- Security: report secrets by type and location only; never include value in comments, check-run summaries, or logs.
- Use concise imperative commit subjects; keep commits small, one coherent validated slice each.
- Pull requests state what changed, any behaviour change, and how it was verified.
